text:
Anna M: Heads up — after the kernel-selector tweak landed in canary we're seeing a p99 jump on long-context text-gen under load. Baseline p99 ~220ms, canary p99 ~410ms. Short traces attached.
Raj P: Was that the autoselect change that prefers mixed-fused kernels for medium sequences? :eyes:
Anna M: Yes. Autoselect chose 'mixed-fused' for 2048 windows. Profile suggests extra kernel fallback at the tail for small microbatches, causing extra init overhead.
Tyler: Can you paste the effective scheduler config from the canary?
Anna M: Config from canary cluster:
```
max_batch_tokens: 4096
max_wait_ms: 8
max_batch_size: 32
microbatch_target_tokens: 256
```

Leo: Noticed KV cache hit rate fell from ~94% -> ~78% on that workload (many long prefixes + short completions). That increases cold kernel runs and per-dispatch cost.
perf-bot: perf summary (canary): p50 18ms -> 20ms, p95 86ms -> 140ms, p99 220ms -> 410ms, tokens/s overall -12%.
Raj P: Looks like max_wait_ms is too low to form stable batches with the new kernel characteristics. More dispatches -> more kernel_init + fallbacks.
Anna M: Hypothesis: kernel switch raised per-dispatch overhead; with mw=8 we emit a lot of tiny dispatches which hit fallback and inflate tail.
Tyler: Proposal: run two quick knobs: increase max_wait_ms to 12-15ms and cap max_batch_tokens to 2048 for this model family. Also test forcing legacy kernel to isolate.
Anna M: Proposed canary command:
```
./run_canary --set max_wait_ms=15 --set max_batch_tokens=2048 --set kernel_prefer=legacy
```

Leo: I'll run an A/B: A = legacy kernel + mw=15/mbt=2048, B = autoselect kernel but mw=25. Want to see trade-offs: A should reduce p99, B might get higher throughput but risk tail.
Raj P: Also capture these metrics per-dispatch: dispatch_size_histogram, kv_hit_rate_histogram, per_dispatch_wall_ms, kernel_init_count. Need tail traces (flamegraphs).
perf-bot: scheduled perf job run_id=1823456805 (10m loadgen, p95 load profile). Uploading profiles when done.
deploy-bot: rolling canary started on cluster r-infer-12: 10% -> 50% traffic, will pause/rollback on regressions.
Anna M: Uploaded flamegraph: https://perf.internal/runs/1823456805/flamegraph.svg — main hotspot shows repeated kernel_init calls for dispatches under ~512 tokens.
Tyler: If kernel_init is ~1.8ms and avg dispatches per request rose from 1 -> 3, avg adds ~3.6ms but p99 multiplies because some requests do many tiny dispatches.
Leo: KV fragmentation seen in trace: many small cache keys due to prefix sharding and request patterns. Aggregating small prefixes should improve hit rate.
Raj P: Agreed. Add a microbatching heuristic: prefer grouping requests with prefix lengths within +/-128 tokens and prefer dispatches that maintain KV locality. That should raise KV hit% and reduce cold kernel triggers.
Anna M: Can we sample detailed dispatch logs for 5% of traffic for 24h? Need raw dispatch sizes + kernel choice + kv_hit flag.
Tyler: I'll enable sampling: `trace.dispatch_size.sample_rate=0.05` and `trace.kv.hit_details=1`.
perf-bot: job complete — preliminary numbers: mw=15, mbt=2048, kernel=legacy -> p99 260ms (from 410ms), throughput -4%, KV hit ~90%. Full artifacts: https://perf.internal/runs/1823456810/
Anna M: Promising. Let's run longer (1h) and check p99/p999 stability and cost impact. If stable, promote and then tune the kernel selector heuristics.
Leo: I'll open a follow-up PR for: (1) microbatch grouping by prefix-length, (2) KV prefix aggregation experiment, (3) additional dispatch logging.
Anna M: Filing tracking epic SRE-2107 to cover rollback/heuristic work + KV aggregation. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Raj P: Also add a perf regression alert on p99 > 300ms for this model family so we auto-pause canaries next time.
Tyler: Will add alert and a short runbook note.
Anna M: Closing loop — keep updates in the canary thread and drop artifacts here.
